questions.question: The SI unit of luminous flux is?
questions.tutor: Lumen (lm) measures total visible light emitted by a source.

questions.question: The SI unit of illuminance (light on a surface) is?
questions.tutor: Lux = lumens per square meter (lm/m²).

questions.question: One foot-candle is equivalent to how many lux?
questions.tutor: 1 fc = 1 lm/ft² = 10.76 lux; 1 lux = 0.0929 fc.

questions.question: The luminous intensity of a source in a given direction is measured in?
questions.tutor: Candela (cd) is the base SI unit for luminous intensity.

questions.question: The efficacy of a lamp is expressed as?
questions.tutor: Efficacy measures how efficiently a lamp converts electrical power into visible light.

questions.question: Which lamp has the highest luminous efficacy among common types?
questions.tutor: HPS lamps achieve 100-150 lm/W; LEDs 80-200 lm/W depending on type.

questions.question: A 100 W incandescent lamp typically produces how many lumens?
questions.tutor: Incandescent efficacy is 12-17 lm/W; 100 W gives about 1200-1700 lm.

questions.question: The color rendering index (CRI) measures?
choices: How accurately colors appear under a light source
questions.tutor: CRI (0-100) compares color appearance to natural sunlight (CRI=100).

questions.question: A lamp with high CRI is preferred for?
questions.tutor: High CRI (≥80) is needed where accurate color perception matters.

questions.question: Correlated color temperature (CCT) of a warm white LED is approximately?
questions.tutor: 2700-3000 K gives yellowish warm light; 5000-6500 K gives cool daylight.

questions.question: Daylight (noon sun) has a color temperature around?
questions.tutor: Noon sunlight is approximately 5600 K; cloudy sky can be 6500-8000 K.

questions.question: The inverse square law for illuminance states that illuminance is?
choices: Inversely proportional to square of distance
questions.tutor: E = I / d² for point source; doubling distance reduces illuminance to 1/4.

questions.question: The cosine law of illumination states that illuminance on a surface is proportional to?
choices: Cosine of angle between light ray and surface normal
questions.tutor: E = (I / d²) × cos θ, where θ is angle from perpendicular.

questions.question: A point source of 500 cd is at 2 meters from a surface. The illuminance normal to the ray is?
questions.tutor: E = I / d² = 500 / 4 = 125 lux (assuming perpendicular incidence).

questions.question: The recommended illuminance for office desk work (general) is?
questions.tutor: IESNA recommends 500 lux for office work; 300-500 for general tasks.

questions.question: The main advantage of LED lamps over fluorescent is?
choices: Longer life, no mercury, instant start
questions.tutor: LEDs last 25,000-100,000 hours, contain no mercury, and start instantly even in cold.

questions.question: A fluorescent lamp requires a ballast to?
choices: Limit current and provide starting voltage
questions.tutor: Ballast provides high starting voltage and limits operating current after arc strikes.

questions.question: Electronic ballasts are preferred over magnetic ballasts because?
questions.tutor: Electronic ballasts operate at high frequency (20-60 kHz), eliminating flicker and improving efficacy.

questions.question: Glare in lighting design is caused by?
questions.tutor: Glare causes visual discomfort from direct or reflected high brightness.

questions.question: The coefficient of utilization (CU) in lighting design accounts for?
choices: Light reaching workplane vs. lamp output
questions.tutor: CU (0-1) depends on room geometry, surface reflectances, and luminaire efficiency.

questions.question: The lumen method formula for average illuminance is?
questions.tutor: E = (lumens per lamp × number of lamps × CU × light loss factor) / area in m².

questions.question: Light loss factor (LLF) includes factors such as?
choices: Lamp lumen depreciation, dirt accumulation, voltage variation
questions.tutor: LLF accounts for lumen depreciation over time and environmental factors.

questions.question: The main purpose of a lighting control system is?
questions.tutor: Controls include occupancy sensors, daylight harvesting, dimming, and scheduling.

questions.question: Daylight harvesting uses photosensors to?
choices: Dim electric lights when daylight is sufficient
questions.tutor: Daylight harvesting reduces energy consumption by automatically adjusting artificial lighting.

questions.question: The life rating of an LED lamp typically refers to?
choices: Time until lumen output drops to 70% (L70)
questions.tutor: L70 (50,000-100,000 hours) means 70% of initial lumens remain, not catastrophic failure.
